public_rationale: OpenAI documented physics failures in February 2024 and explicitly acknowledged unrealistic physics in the version released that December. These primary records support the ordinary reading that Sora's physics problems had not gone away by the retrospective's publication.
limitations: The evidence establishes persistence, not a measured failure rate or an absence of improvement.
This assessment does not verify the date or exact wording of Marcus's original prediction.
The launch page contains later availability notices; the cited passage describes the December 2024 deployment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Sora's troubles with physics have not gone away since its February 2024 announcement.

statement.excerpt: Immediately after the February announcement of Sora, I noted Sora’s troubles with physics and predicted that they wouldn’t go away. They haven’t.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: predicted that they wouldn’t go away
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that physically unrealistic behavior remained a limitation of Sora at the end of 2024.
This retrospective does not assert that every output violates physics or that Sora made no improvements.
The target runs from the February 2024 announcement through December 2024, as specified by the retrospective context.
I assess the stated persistence of the limitation, rather than treating the recalled prediction as an unlimited forecast about all future Sora models.
criteria.support_condition: Primary documentation or reproducible observations establish physics failures in the February model and show that the limitation remained in the late-2024 version.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that the relevant physics failures had been resolved in the version available by the end of 2024. Improved speed or selected successful videos alone would not suffice.
